H1.maths: sweep value over 1,000,000 ordinary x 1,000,000 raw bit patterns x 33 specials, x 4 limits, count where (x > limit) differs from !(x <= limit)
H1.not_claimed: This settles a comparison, not a design. It says nothing about whether the limits themselves are right and nothing about any physics.
H1.question: Does a verdict ever report a value it cannot justify as inside a rating?
H1.settled: SETTLED: on every finite number the two forms agree exactly (0 disagreements), so this changes no real design; they part only where the value is not a number, and there the live form reports 1,001,580 passes it cannot justify across 4 limits.

H2.maths: sweep beta -0.30..-0.20 x series 20..34 x temperature -20..0 C x 10 module bins, count where N*Voc*(1+beta/100*(T-25)) > 1500
H2.not_claimed: This settles where a printed Voc and a printed coefficient put the string voltage. It does not settle the site's design minimum temperature, which is a meteorological input this file does not hold, and it does not model the rise of Voc with irradiance, which makes the real answer worse rather than better.
H2.question: Where does the series string cross the 1500 V rating, and how much of the answer depends on which temperature coefficient is paired with which Voc?
H2.settled: SETTLED: 460,863 of 1,227,150 cases cross 1500 V on each bin's own printed coefficient, and the exact crossing temperature is solved for every bin and series count; 23,929 cases turn on WHICH coefficient is used, which is the whole of the earlier mistake.

axes.name: symbol pieces
axes.range: 0..96, matched by a PREFIX test on the tag

smallest_starving_count.note: the count at which the floors first exceed the budget, so the rounding loop cannot give every piece its floor and a piece receives zero dots

H3.maths: sweep pieces 1..384 x symbols 0..96 x symbol rings 0..96 x plain rings 0..96, count where SR*16 + (S-SR)*6 + NR*5 + (P-S-NR)*2 > 896
H3.not_claimed: This settles the arithmetic of the floors against the budget. It does not say which real drawings reach those shapes, and it does not check that a piece given its floor is legible - only that it is given something.
H3.question: Can a drawing ask for more floor dots than the budget holds, so that a piece of it is drawn with nothing?
H3.settled: SETTLED: of 125,864,192 real shapes, 98,231,558 leave the floors alone over the 896 dot budget, so a piece of the drawing is handed zero dots; 57 symbol rings on their own are enough to do it.

at_the_sheets_own_top_rear_row.condition: 25 C, the condition the row is printed for

H4.maths: sweep rear gain 0..30% x temperature -20..25 C x series 20..34 x 10 bins, count where Imp*(1+phi*rear)*(1+alpha/100*(T-25)) > 20 or 1.25*Isc*(1+phi*rear)*(1+alpha/100*(T-25))*2 > 40
H4.not_claimed: This settles current against two printed input ratings. It does not model non-uniform rear illumination along a string, the transient, or the fact that high albedo and low ambient are the same weather - which means the joint corner is present in the count but its real likelihood is understated by reading either axis on its own.
H4.question: Where does rear-side irradiance take the string current past the string and machine inputs?
H4.settled: SETTLED: 292,950 of 832,650 cases exceed the 20 A string input and 832,650 the 40 A machine input; at the sheet's own 25% rear row EVERY bin exceeds both.

house_rule: Every finding carries two implementations of the same sum - a kernel on the card and a reference on the processor - and is probed against itself before any count is reported. A finding whose implementations differ is reported FAILING and its counts are withheld.
not_claimed: The crunch settles ARITHMETIC over a stated space and nothing else. It does not decide whether the stated space is the right space, whether the predicate is the right question, or whether a count that comes back zero means the concern was unfounded rather than the sweep too narrow. It holds no site, no weather record and no as-built drawing, so it cannot say any of these findings is present in a real installation - only that the numbers in the files reach it. Fixes, costs and priority are not settled here at all: a count is evidence for a person to act on, not the action.
